newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-FORD END 31-YEAR DAYTONA DROUGHT.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FORD END 31-YEAR DAYTONA DROUGHT.

text.p: A six-driver team of four Americans and two Britons gave Ford its first outright victory in the Daytona 24 Hours sportscar race since 1966 on Sunday.
Britons James Weaver and Andy Wallace, sharing with Rob Dyson, Butch Leitzinger, John Paul Jr and Elliot Forbes Robinson snatched victory by one lap.

The Ford ran the final hour with smoke pouring from a broken piston but still covered a race distance of 690 laps (2456 miles/3953 km). "The motor kept getting worse and worse. It started making some noises and lost a lot of power," said Leitzinger.
Second place went to the Ferrari of Spain's Fermin Velez and Americans Andy Evans and father-and-son Charles and Rob Morgan.
The Ferrari led early on but was delayed by several collisions, one in which Rob Morgan and Weaver went spinning off the track.
It was the second Daytona victory for Wallace -- he won there in 1990 for Jaguar -- but the first 24-hour triumph in more than 15 years of trying for Weaver.
"Perhaps I had better stick to driving with Andy instead of against him as I have been for years," said Weaver.
The weekend was overshadowed by the death of a driver in a special two-hour IMSA Endurance championship race on Friday.
Michael Himes of Los Gatos, California, was killed when he crashed his Honda Del Sol on the combined banked and road circuit, according to a statement from the Daytona International Speedway.
